codeReview.summary: Solid AES-256-GCM crypto implementation covering all 5 required functions. The code is well-structured with clear section dividers, proper JSDoc, and correct error handling (never throws, returns null or {error}). The IV:AuthTag:CipherText format is correctly implemented with proper GCM parameters (12-byte IV, 16-byte auth tag). Tests are comprehensive (58 tests) covering happy paths, edge cases, roundtrip, file I/O, and permissions. All expectedBehavior items from the feature spec are satisfied. Three minor non-blocking issues found.

issues.description: Unused import: `chmodSync` is imported from `node:fs` but never used in the module. File permissions are handled by `writeFileAtomic` from `./fs.js` which has its own `chmodSync` import. This is dead code.

Module docstring says 'Dependencies: constants (for path defaults), fs (for atomic writes)' but `constants.js` is never imported. The module only depends on `node:crypto`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, and `./fs.js`. The comment is misleading.

The inner try/catch around `Buffer.from(trimmedKey, 'base64')` (lines 47-49 in decryptAuthV2, and similarly in encryptAuthV2) will never catch: Node.js `Buffer.from(string, 'base64')` silently ignores invalid characters rather than throwing. The actual validation is handled by the subsequent key length check (`keyBuf.length !== 32`), which works correctly as a proxy. The try/catch is misleading but harmless.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker noted that the TDD skill's 'Write Tests First (RED)' phase doesn't work for brand new modules because barrel re-exports and the module file must exist before tests can even be loaded/parsed by Bun. The skill could clarify that creating a stub module and barrel re-exports is a prerequisite step before the RED phase when building new modules.

summary: The factory-crypto feature is well-implemented and passes review. All 5 functions (decryptAuthV2, encryptAuthV2, generateAuthKey, readAuthV2Files, writeAuthV2Files) are correctly implemented with proper AES-256-GCM cryptography, comprehensive error handling, and secure file permissions. 58 tests provide thorough coverage including roundtrip verification, edge cases (null, empty, wrong segment count, wrong key length, corrupt ciphertext, trailing whitespace), and file I/O with permission checks. Three non-blocking issues identified: an unused chmodSync import, a misleading module docstring referencing an unimported constants dependency, and a try/catch around Buffer.from(base64) that can never actually catch (since Node.js silently handles invalid base64). None of these affect correctness or security.
